walkthroughs.body_html: According to the Torah and Bible, God gave Moses ten commandments on Mount Sinai. They include: worship only God, honour your parents, do not murder, do not steal, do not lie, and do not be jealous of others' things.
The Ten Commandments are shared by Jews and Christians, and have influenced laws in many countries. They set out basic ideas of justice, honesty and respect that still shape society today.

Philosophers use ethical theories to decide what is right. Utilitarianism says do whatever creates the greatest happiness. Deontology says follow moral rules even if results are bad. Virtue ethics says focus on being a good person.

mcqs.q: Is the Buddha a god in Buddhism?
options: Natural evil means evil that is good for nature.

No — the Buddha (Siddhartha Gautama) is regarded as an enlightened human teacher who discovered the path to liberation. Theravada Buddhism is generally non-theistic; some Mahayana traditions develop more elaborate cosmologies.
The Buddha created the universe.
Buddhists worship the Buddha as their god.

mcqs.q: What distinction matters for the free will defence to the problem of evil?
options: Natural evil means evil that is good for nature.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
The free will defence solves all forms of evil at once.

Between moral evil (caused by free human choices) and natural evil (earthquakes, disease) — the free will defence directly addresses moral evil but struggles with natural evil, which isn't a product of free choice.

mcqs.q: What is the problem of evil?
options: It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.
Natural evil means evil that is good for nature.
If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
